newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican teachers win wage hike on eve of marches.
newsitem.headline: Mexican teachers win wage hike on eve of marches.

text.p: Mexican teachers won a wage and benefits increase on Wednesday that totalled 16 percent, on the eve of mass marches planned for Teachers Day, Education Minister Miguel Limon Rojas said.
The increase included a 6 percent rise on basic salaries and a 10 percent increase in benefits, and adds to a 17 percent increase in January.

The total 33 percent rise is slightly more than last year, and Limon Rojas noted on national television late Wednesday that inflation this year is expected to fall to 15 percent from 27.7 percent last year.
But Mexican workers complain they are still grossly underpaid, earning what news reports say is an average $11 per day -- just three times the minimum wage.

Protests by anti-government teachers unions have become a spring ritual in the capital and across southern Mexico ahead of Teachers Day. On Wednesday, Mexico City traffic was clogged for hours by protesting teachers, and more protests were planned for Thursday.
